title: Close a named ball valve and lock it with a clamp-on ball valve lockout and a padlock
instruction: Close ball valve V-12: turn its handle a quarter turn clockwise, seen from above, until it points at you. Fit the red valve lockout over the handle and the valve, with the handle inside its channel and its legs on both sides of the pipe, and push its two halves together. Then put your padlock's shackle through the lined-up hole in the side of the lockout and snap it shut. Do not operate valve V-14.
context: Isolating a line for maintenance means closing its valve and locking it closed. A valve whose handle has no lock hole is locked with a clamp-on lockout over the handle; closing the wrong valve, or leaving the lockout unpadlocked, lets the line be reopened onto a worker.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top. Pipe run: a 1/2 in schedule-40 steel pipe (21.3 mm outside diameter, 48 cm long) runs left-right, its axis 26 cm in front of the bases and 9.0 cm above the table, from 12 cm right to 36 cm left of the midline, fixed to the table on two grey plastic stands (3 x 2 cm columns on 8 x 5 x 0.8 cm feet) at 9 cm right and 33 cm left of the midline. Valves: two Milwaukee Valve BA-100 1/2 in bronze two-piece threaded ball valves with the standard lever (body 56 mm end to end), stems 26 cm in front of the bases: V-12 on the midline, V-14 25 cm left of it. Each lever is flat steel (97 x 16 x 2.5 mm, 50 g, yellow vinyl grip 19 x 6 mm on its outer 52 mm), 13.5 cm above the table, turning about the vertical stem between its two stops. Both valves are open, levers pointing right along the pipe; closed, a lever points straight at the robot. Valve tags: each valve has an engraved two-ply plastic tag (102 x 51 x 1.6 mm, white face, black letters about 28 mm tall reading V-12 or V-14) on an 8 mm steel strap clamped round the pipe 5 cm left of its stem; tag centre 8 cm behind the stem, 1.5 cm right of it and 12 cm above the table, long side left-right, face tilted back 60 degrees from vertical toward the robot. Lockout: a Master Lock S3080 adjustable ball valve lockout (red; 134.6 x 76.9 x 104.1 mm, 156 g; half A is a channel with a pair of legs at its far end, half B a second pair of legs with a housing of four lock holes that slides on A's tongue, on the device's right side). It stands on its four legs on the table 15 cm left of the midline with its channel pointing at the robot and its lock-hole housing on its right, opened so its two leg pairs are 4.0 cm apart (A's legs 12.9 to 13.9 cm, B's legs 17.9 to 18.9 cm in front of the bases); the channel's near end rests on a grey plastic block (3 x 5 cm, 7.1 cm tall) 8 cm in front of the bases. Padlock: a Master Lock 410 Zenex safety padlock (purple, 410PRP; body 38 x 45 x 19 mm, 6.35 mm shackle with 38 mm vertical and 19 mm horizontal clearance; 0.10 kg), open (shackle popped out 16 mm), lies on its side in a grey plastic cradle (5 x 4 cm, 6 cm tall, with 6 mm lips either side of the body) 20 cm in front of the bases and 17 cm right of the midline, shackle pointing left and the short leg below the long one. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Score 0 if, at any time, V-14's lever turns 10 degrees or more, or V-12's lever, once closed, goes back more than 30 degrees from closed before the after-release check. Otherwise the score is the highest level reached: 0.25 if V-12's lever has turned 10 degrees or more toward closed; 0.5 if it reaches closed (within 5 degrees of its stop, pointing at the robot); 0.75 if, with the lever closed, the lockout is fitted (the lever in its channel, the device resting on the lever within 4 mm and 8 degrees of its fitted position, A's legs in front of the pipe and B's behind it) and its halves are pushed together to the first setting (within 2 mm); 1.0 if, in addition, the padlock's shackle is shut through the lined-up holes of B's housing and A's tongue and the after-release check passes. Dropping the padlock or the lockout is not penalised by itself. After-release check, done once both grippers have been at least 6 cm from the padlock and from V-12's stem for 2 s: pull the lockout's two halves apart along the lever with a spring scale on each (15 N on A toward the robot, 15 N on B away from it) and keep pulling; after 2 s also push V-12's lever toward open with 3.0 N m (42 N at the grip's centre, 71 mm from the stem) for 2 s. Pass if the lever stays within 15 degrees of closed and the shackle is still through the holes; if not, the score is 0.75. Angles are read from a photo taken from above with a protractor template.
reset_notes: Open the padlock with its key and remove it; slide the lockout's halves apart, lift it off and stand it back on its legs at its mark, opened to 4.0 cm, channel on its block; turn V-12's lever back to open (pointing right); check V-14 is open; lay the open padlock back in its cradle, shackle pointing left, short leg down. About 2 minutes.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies on joints, arms with the station's i2rt gains. The lock is all geometry: lever held in the lockout's channel, legs astride the pipe, shackle through both halves' holes. Lever friction 1.0 N·m (Milwaukee: 4.5 N·m at full pressure) so one arm can turn it. Lockout internals (holes, walls, tongue) inferred from photos; box colliders; no clamp preload, so lift-off is not checked; padlock latches by a catch, no key. Details in README.
